newsitem.title: USA: Lott offers compromise on U.S. disaster aid bill.
newsitem.headline: Lott offers compromise on U.S. disaster aid bill.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott on Tuesday offered to compromise with the White House and pass a $2 billion to $3 billion bill providing emergency disaster aid as well as funds for U.S. troops in Bosnia and the Persian Gulf.
Speaking to reporters, the Mississippi Republican said later in the year Congress would then consider a separate bill with the remainder of the funds and policies sought by Republicans.
President Clinton vetoed the full $8.6 billion spending bill over Republican provisions to avert a government shutdown and change the method of taking the census.

Senate Minority Leader Tom Daschle Tuesday blocked the Senate from debating other legislation until action is taken on emergency disaster relief for several states. "We are going to object to any other piece of legislation," the South Dakota Democrat said on the Senate floor.
Lott said he would allow the Senate to remain in session late into the night for Republican and Democratic speeches on the disaster relief bill or other issues.
Lott told reporters the second supplemental appropriations bill would still contain enough funds "to keep the pressure on us and the president."
